symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries in the source vector, the length of the transform being replaced.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ be the number of entries in the source vector, the transform being replaced, and $t$ the number of entries in the resampled vector, a power of two greater than $s$.

symbols.name: resampled length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries in the resampled vector, a power of two greater than $s$.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ be the number of entries in the source vector, the transform being replaced, and $t$ the number of entries in the resampled vector, a power of two greater than $s$.

symbols.name: halving count
symbols.meaning: The number of halvings of a transform length, so that the length is $2^\ell$.
symbols.quote: The count $\ell$ is the number of halvings, so a length is $2^\ell$.

symbols.name: Gaussian width
symbols.meaning: The integer width of the Gaussian weights.
symbols.quote: A Gaussian weight is $e^{-\pi x^2/\alpha^2}$ for a real number $x$, where $e$ is the base of the natural logarithm and the integer $\alpha$ is the width: the weight is near 1 when $x$ is small against $\alpha$ and near 0 otherwise.

symbols.name: relative gap
symbols.meaning: The relative gap $t/s-1$ between the two lengths.
symbols.quote: Let $\theta = t/s-1$ be the relative gap between the two lengths.

symbols.name: generic source vector
symbols.meaning: A generic vector of length $s$, on which $P_s$ acts.
symbols.quote: Let $u$ be a generic vector of length $s$, $v$ one of length $t$, and $j$, $k$ positions; these letters are reused here.

symbols.name: generic resampled vector
symbols.meaning: A generic vector of length $t$, on which $P_t$ acts.
symbols.quote: Let $u$ be a generic vector of length $s$, $v$ one of length $t$, and $j$, $k$ positions; these letters are reused here.

symbols.name: source position
symbols.meaning: An index position of a length-$s$ vector, running from $0$ to $s-1$ in the permutation.
symbols.quote: Let $u$ be a generic vector of length $s$, $v$ one of length $t$, and $j$, $k$ positions; these letters are reused here.

symbols.name: resampled position
symbols.meaning: An index position of a length-$t$ vector in the permutation $P_t$.
symbols.quote: Let $u$ be a generic vector of length $s$, $v$ one of length $t$, and $j$, $k$ positions; these letters are reused here.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of length-$s$ vectors defined by $(P_s u)_j = u_{tj \bmod s}$.
symbols.quote: Define the coordinate permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ by $(P_s u)_j = u_{tj \bmod s}$ and $(P_t v)_k = v_{-sk \bmod t}$.

symbols.name: resampled permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of length-$t$ vectors defined by $(P_t v)_k = v_{-sk \bmod t}$.
symbols.quote: Define the coordinate permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ by $(P_s u)_j = u_{tj \bmod s}$ and $(P_t v)_k = v_{-sk \bmod t}$.

symbols.name: map into length t
symbols.meaning: A linear contraction from length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors, in the identity.
symbols.quote: Here $E$ maps length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors, and $U$ maps length-$t$ vectors back to length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: map back to s
symbols.meaning: A linear contraction from length-$t$ vectors to length-$s$ vectors, in the identity.
symbols.quote: Here $E$ maps length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors, and $U$ maps length-$t$ vectors back to length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: first resampling map
symbols.meaning: One of the two maps from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors used in the proof.
symbols.quote: Here $\Sigma$ and $\Gamma$ are maps from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors, each output entry a Gaussian-weighted sum of input entries.

symbols.name: second resampling map
symbols.meaning: The other of the two maps from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors used in the proof.
symbols.quote: Here $\Sigma$ and $\Gamma$ are maps from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors, each output entry a Gaussian-weighted sum of input entries.

symbols.name: near-identity map
symbols.meaning: A map built from $\Gamma$ and Gaussian corrections, close to the identity.
symbols.quote: Let $N$ be the map built from $\Gamma$ and Gaussian corrections.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling replaces a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length by a transform whose length is a power of two. It reshapes the transforms of the [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) into [multidimensional transforms](multidimensional-transform.md) with power-of-two axes, so that the later steps can use butterfly layers and polynomial transforms.

It reshapes the transforms of the [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) into [multidimensional transforms](multidimensional-transform.md) with power-of-two axes, so that the later steps can use butterfly layers and polynomial transforms.

Gaussian resampling replaces a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length by a transform whose length is a power of two. It reshapes the transforms of the [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) into [multidimensional transforms](multidimensional-transform.md) with power-of-two axes, so that the later steps can use butterfly layers and polynomial transforms.
Gaussian resampling converts the lengths for the [synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transforms.md) into powers of two.
Gaussian resampling requires that $s$ and $t$ be [coprime](coprime.md), $\gcd(s,t)=1$.
